evals.prompt: `npm run typecheck` in scope/ (a small pricing library) is slower than it should be and keeps growing. Find out what the compiler is actually checking and trim it, but the same `tsc -p .` must keep checking everything in src/ and the tests in test/. Show before and after numbers. Install typescript from scope/package.json if you need it.
evals.expected_output: tsc --listFilesOnly/--explainFiles and --extendedDiagnostics show the program pulls in fixtures/generated/payloads.ts and the stale dist/index.d.ts through include **/*; the include is scoped to src and test (or those folders are excluded), the typecheck still passes, and Files/Types/Check time are reported before and after with the same flags.

assertions.text: `tsc -p . --listFilesOnly` still lists every src/ file and the test file, and no longer lists fixtures/generated/ or dist/

assertions.check:
command -v node >/dev/null || { echo "node not installed"; exit 1; }
TSC=""
for c in "${TSC_BIN:-}" "$PWD/scope/node_modules/.bin/tsc" "$PWD/node_modules/.bin/tsc" "$(command -v tsc 2>/dev/null)"; do
  if [ -n "$c" ] && [ -x "$c" ]; then TSC="$c"; break; fi
done
[ -n "$TSC" ] || { echo "tsc not found: install typescript in scope/ or set TSC_BIN"; exit 1; }
cd scope || exit 1
"$TSC" -p .

assertions.text: The tests still pass under node --test

assertions: The reply reports compiler counters (Files, Types or Lines, and Check time from --extendedDiagnostics) for the same command before and after the change, and shows what attributed the extra files (--listFilesOnly or --explainFiles output).

evals.prompt: tsc --noEmit on our monorepo takes 3 minutes and the machine has 16 cores. I tried `--checkers 8` and `Types` went down but Check time barely moved. Decide whether my type change helped or not, and tell me how to compare fairly. Nothing is checked out; answer from the approach.
evals.expected_output: Explains that on tsc 7 Types and Memory used vary with the checker count, so baseline and candidate must be measured with --singleThreaded (or the same --checkers N) on the same tsc version, with .tsbuildinfo deleted; then uses --generateTrace with analyze-trace to attribute Check time before changing types.
assertions: The reply says Types or Memory used change with --checkers on tsc 7 and compares only runs with --singleThreaded or an identical --checkers value and tsc version
The reply says to delete .tsbuildinfo (or avoid incremental) before cold measurements
The reply attributes the slow check with --extendedDiagnostics and --generateTrace (analyze-trace) before editing types

evals.prompt: Declaration emit for packages/shared takes most of our build and blocks the apps. A teammate says to set `isolatedDeclarations: true` in tsconfig and we will get faster builds. Advise, and show the exact config and commands. Nothing is checked out.
evals.expected_output: States that the flag alone brings no speedup: it requires explicit annotations on every export (TS90xx errors otherwise), and the gain comes from emitting declarations without type-checking (--noCheck or a separate declaration emitter) alongside a separate tsc --noEmit that still reports type errors; also suggests project references with tsc -b.
assertions: The reply says isolatedDeclarations alone does not speed up tsc and that unannotated exports fail with TS90xx errors
The reply pairs declaration emit without checking (--noCheck or a separate emitter) with a separate tsc --noEmit so type errors are still reported
The reply does not widen exported types (any, object) to satisfy the flag

evals.prompt: Check time in our tsc run is dominated by .d.ts files. Add skipLibCheck to fix it. We also keep hand-written ambient declarations in types/*.d.ts. Nothing is checked out.
evals.expected_output: Confirms by comparing --extendedDiagnostics with and without --skipLibCheck, warns that skipLibCheck also skips the project's own hand-written .d.ts files and can hide conflicts, and keeps a separate job or one-off run without the flag.
assertions: The reply measures Check time or Types with and without skipLibCheck before recommending it
The reply warns that skipLibCheck also skips the hand-written types/*.d.ts files and can hide conflicts
The reply keeps one check without the flag (a separate job or a one-off diff of errors)
